findings.title: Dwelling places remain as visible witness
findings.claim: The plural possessed dwelling term can carry a global ruin-witness resonance: places once inhabited remain visible evidence after a people is destroyed.
findings.mechanism: The local source phrase makes the dwellings the material origin of clarity; 46:25 says that after destruction only the dwellings are seen, while 27:52 shows emptied houses and calls the scene a sign.
findings.reader_payoff: Ruined houses become readable testimony rather than background scenery.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning remains their dwellings. Stillness and surviving witness are contextual resonance, not a replacement gloss, etymology, or claim about every surviving building.

epistemic.reason: The candidate and lexical supports are trusted, and both wider Arabic records directly supply the dwelling-remnant scenes.

evidence_facts.fact: مَسَاكِنِهِمْ names possessed plural dwelling-places; the root range includes dwelling, settling, repose, and stillness.
مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ is a plural noun in the genitive under مِن and carries a third-person plural possessive suffix.
46:25 places destruction before the statement that only their dwellings are seen.
27:52 presents their houses as empty because of wrongdoing and calls that scene a sign for people who know.
The registered focus branch gloss is bir yere yerleşip orada yaşama.
